items.title: Novo’s Wegovy pill helps patients lose about 6% of weight in three months, real-world data show
items.author: Reuters Staff
items.summary: Patients who stayed on Novo Nordisk’s daily Wegovy pill lost an average of 6.2 per cent of their body weight over three months, according to real-world data due to be presented at the ObesityWeek ...
items.body: LONDON -- Patients who stayed on Novo Nordisk’s daily Wegovy pill lost an average of 6.2 per cent of their body weight over three months, according to real-world data due to be presented at the ObesityWeek conference in Washington. The pill, launched in January, has helped Novo regain some ground lost to Eli Lilly, and the Danish drugmaker is trying to stay ahead of its U.S. rival in the race for oral obesity treatments. Novo’s Chief Scientific Officer Martin Holst Lange said in an interview that the real-world data was encouraging as it broadly replicated the findings of 5.5 per cent weight loss at 12 weeks seen in Novo’s late-stage trial for the pill. Study participants, who started taking the pill between January 5 and February 7, 2026, lost an average of 6.3 kg (13.9 pounds) from a baseline weight of 103.0 kg (227 pounds), Novo said. About three-fifths lost at least 5 per cent of their weight, and roughly one in six lost at least 10 per cent. The analysis covered 5,872 adults on the Ro telehealth platform who had never taken a weight-loss drug and who stayed on the pill for the full three months. Novo Nordisk’s fortunes have declined significantly since it became Europe’s most valuable listed company following the 2021 launch of its injectable weight-loss drug, Wegovy. Its stock has plummeted over 70 per cent from its peak as Lilly surpassed it to take the lead in the obesity-drug market. According to company presentations earlier this month, however, oral treatments now represent roughly a third of U.S. obesity prescriptions, with Novo securing over 80 per cent of new oral prescriptions. The company in September said separate real-world data showed patients who switched from weight-loss injections to Novo’s pill continued to lose weight. Oral Wegovy — known chemically as semaglutide — led to about a 14 per cent reduction in body weight over 64 weeks, while Eli Lilly’s obesity pill Foundayo led to about an 11 per cent reduction over 72 weeks, separate studies have shown. Reporting by Patrick Wingrove in London; Editing by Tomasz Janowski, Reuters

items.title: スペースＸ「スターシップ」、発射塔のアームで上段部分の初回収に成功　完全再利用へ前進
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［米テキサス州スターベース　１４日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［米テキサス州スターベース　１４日　ロイター］ - 米実業家イーロン・マスク氏率いる宇宙開発企業スペースＸの次世代ロケット「スターシップ」が１４日、２２時間の地球周回軌道飛行から帰還し、テキサス州の発射塔に設置された巨大なアームによってロケットの上段部分が初めて回収された。今回の回収成功は、同社が１０年かけて開発を進めてきた完全再利用可能なロケットにとって不可欠なものとみられている。

スターシップは２６基のスターリンク衛星を軌道上に展開。上段部分は地球を１４周した後、同州スターベースにあるスペースＸの発射場上空の厚い雲の中から姿を現した。機体を垂直に反転させるためエンジンを再点火し、轟音を立てながら、発射塔に設置された「メカジラ」と呼ばれるアームに向かってゆっくり降下した。

下段部分の回収には失敗した。

マスク氏は、スターシップをスペースＸの収益性の高いスターリンク衛星事業の将来の主力機と見なしており、軌道上にデータセンターを設置したり、人類を月へ帰還させたり、最終的には火星に定住させたりといった野望を実現するための重要な手段と位置付けている。

items.title: サッカー＝国際親善試合で日本がブラジルに競り勝つ、坂元が決勝点
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［１４日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［１４日　ロイター］ - サッカーの日本代表は１４日、シンガポールで国際親善試合を行い、ブラジル代表に３─２で競り勝った。後半アディショナルタイムに坂元達裕が決勝ゴールを奪った。

世界ランキング１７位の日本は前半１５分、堂安律のスルーパスで抜け出した久保建英が左足で決めて先制。さらにその４分後、右サイドからの中野就斗のクロスを受けた中村敬斗がゴール隅に流し込み、世界ランク６位の相手を２─０とリードした。

日本は同３３分と後半３０分にビニシウス・ジュニオールにゴールを決められて追い付かれたが、途中出場の坂元がアディショナルタイム１分に決勝ゴール。南野拓実のブロックの後、こぼれ球を拾った佐野海舟が持ち込み、最後はゴール前の混戦の中で坂元が浮かせたシュートを決めた。

日本は６月に行われたワールドカップ（Ｗ杯）北中米３カ国大会の決勝トーナメント１回戦では、ブラジルに１─２の逆転負けを喫していた。日本は１７日にパラグアイと対戦。８年余りチームを指揮した森保一監督は、この試合を最後に退任する。

items.title: 野球＝日本が豪州に七回コールド勝ちで決勝進出、アジアプロ野球
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［１４日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［１４日　ロイター］ - 野球のアジアプロ野球チャンピオンシップは１４日、東京ドームで１次リーグの２試合を行い、日本はオーストラリアに１６─１で圧勝。七回コールドゲームで３連勝として決勝に進んだ。

日本は一回表に打者１５人の猛攻で一挙１１得点を挙げた。相手のエラーで１点を先制した後、指名打者の山口航輝、渡部聖弥内野手が連続タイムリー。その後も３者連続の押し出し四球などで７─０とし、宗山塁内野手が満塁本塁打でさらにリードを広げた。

二回には正木智也内野手、三回には渡部が２ランを放った。先発の武内夏暉投手は４回を投げて１安打、ソロ本塁打による１失点に抑えた。大会３連覇を目指す日本は１５日の決勝で韓国と対戦する。３位決定戦では台湾とオーストラリアが戦う。

この日のもう１試合では、韓国が台湾に６─４で勝利。オーストラリア、台湾と１勝２敗で並んだが、得失点率差（１イニング当たりの得点率と失点率の差）で韓国が勝ち上がった。

items.title: 米航空便、15日夜に正常化へ　保守作業の不具合原因か
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
David Shepardson

[ワシントン １４日 ロイター] -
items.body:
David Shepardson

[ワシントン １４日 ロイター] - ベッドフォード米連邦航空局（ＦＡＡ）長官は１４日、全米の空港で航空機の離陸が停止された問題について、通常の運航ダイヤに戻るのは１５日夜遅くになるとの見通しを示した。運航は徐々に回復しており、当局は定期保守作業中の不具合が原因だったとしている。

ＦＡＡは１３日、航空管制センターで通信障害が発生したとして、全米の空港で航空機の地上待機命令を発出。航空情報サイトのフライトアウェアによると、同日は約９２００便が欠航、約７５００便が遅延した。米東部時間午後４時１５分（２１１５ＧＭＴ、日本時間１５日午前６時１５分）時点で、１４日の欠航は５３００便超、遅延は約６３００便となった。

ベッドフォード氏は混乱について謝罪するとともに、システムは現時点で安定していると語った。

ホワイトハウスは１３日、危機管理室で緊急会合を開き、連邦政府機関はサイバー攻撃かどうかの確認に追われた。しかし、ダフィー運輸長官は１４日、問題の発端はＦＡＡの請負業者Ｌ３ハリスが遠隔地の施設で少なくとも１台の新しいルーターを設置した作業にあったと説明した。

INDIAN WELLS, California, Nov 14 : Aryna Sabalenka apologised on Saturday for her angry outburst during her defeat by Ukraine's Elina Svitolina at the WTA Finals.
Television footage appeared to show the Belarusian swearing during Friday's round-robin match, with some social media users interpreting her remarks as being directed at Svitolina or Ukrainians. The loss eliminated Sabalenka from the season-ending tournament.
"My comment was not directed at Elina," Sabalenka said in a social media post.
"I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment.

"That said, I should have handled my frustration differently, and I apologise to anyone I offended.
"Elina played a great match, and I wish her all the best for the rest of the tournament."
Svitolina did not shake hands with Sabalenka after the match, maintaining her policy of not doing so with Russian or Belarusian opponents following Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, which Moscow launched with Belarus as a staging ground.
The 2018 WTA Finals champion will play Linda Noskova on Saturday for a place in the final.

items.title: SpaceX’s Starship returns from orbit and is captured by launch pad arms in a dramatic first
items.author: The Associated Press
items.summary: SpaceX’s Starship made a triumphant return to Earth on Saturday, caught in midair by giant mechanical arms where its journey began 22 hours earlier.
items.body: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. — SpaceX’s Starship made a triumphant return to Earth on Saturday, caught in midair by giant mechanical arms where its journey began 22 hours earlier. It was the grand finale that Elon Musk and his team hoped for -- the first-ever capture of a Starship flying back from space. But with the first-stage booster exploding shortly after Friday’s liftoff from Texas, the company fell short of its desired double catch, still the goal for accelerating moon and Mars travel. Wreckage remained in the Gulf of Mexico, cordoned off by buoys, as the stainless steel, bullet-shaped spacecraft lowered itself upright at the launch pad. The dramatic, sci-fi-like capture helped blot out the booster’s messy miss. Cameras panned the spacecraft up and down as it hung high above the ground, supported by the arms of the launch tower. “Can you believe it?” SpaceX commentator Dan Huot shouted, dragging out each word. “Look at her! Baby, she’s back!” Soon afterward, Musk congratulated his “incredible team.” SpaceX officials said Saturday’s catch demonstrates the full reusability of Starship, crucial for rapid and low-cost recycling. Although Friday’s booster recovery failed, the company had already made three previous booster catches, validating the technique. NASA welcomed Saturday’s news. The space agency is paying billions of dollars for Starship to land Artemis astronauts on the moon later this decade and help build a permanent lunar base. Musk’s ambitions are even grander: He wants to launch a fleet of Starships to build a city on Mars. “It was almost magic,” NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said via X. “Making more believers by the day ... one step closer to (emojis of the moon and the U.S. flag).” The world’s largest and most powerful rocket -- a 407-foot (124-metre) behemoth -- blasted off late Friday afternoon from SpaceX’s Starship base near the U.S.-Mexican border. Separating neatly from its booster before things went awry, the upper-stage spacecraft soared into orbit and released 26 advanced Starlink satellites. Starship continued circling the world 165 miles (265 kilometres) up, with live views of itself and Earth streaming down via Starlink. The spacecraft completed 14 laps around Earth, outshining the previous mission’s one to two laps. It was SpaceX’s 15th flight of a full-scale Starship since 2023 and its only second trip to orbit. SpaceX reported that everything on the spacecraft, including its vital heat shield, appeared to work well. As for the booster, SpaceX’s Kate Tice said its engines stopped firing too soon on the way back down. The booster’s guidance system sensed it wasn’t in the right position and automatically initiated the watery detour and self-destruction. Engineers are still investigating the cause. SpaceX expects to begin launching Starships from Florida’s Kennedy Space Center within the next few months. That is the starting point for NASA’s next Artemis mission, which will skip the moon and remain in orbit around Earth for lunar lander practice. Artemis III’s four astronauts will attempt to dock their capsule with not only Starship but Blue Origin’s Blue Moon. The two companies will take turns delivering crews to the lunar surface. NASA is targeting as soon as 2028 for Artemis IV, humanity’s first moon landing since the Apollo era more than half a century ago. Marcia Dunn, The Associated Press

items.title: What Canadians should know about their air passenger rights amid U.S. travel chaos
items.author: The Canadian Press
items.summary: As Canadian airlines and airports continue to deal with the aftershocks of the Friday grounding of U.S. air traffic, some travellers are facing cancellations and delays to their plans.
items.body: As Canadian airlines and airports continue to deal with the aftershocks of the Friday grounding of U.S. air traffic, some travellers are facing cancellations and delays to their plans. Under Canada’s Air Passenger Protection Regulations, passengers have the right to be rebooked if their flight is cancelled or subject to a lengthy delay. Airlines must rebook travellers on the next available flight operated by them or a partner airline that departs within 48 hours of the passenger’s original departure time. Gabor Lukacs, an air passenger rights advocate, says for international travel, like to and from the U.S., if airlines can’t find a flight within that 48-hour period, they are required to rebook passengers on a competing airline. When disruptions are within an airline’s control, passengers are guaranteed more protections and can claim compensation, but Lukacs says that isn’t the case here. The nationwide grounding of U.S. air traffic is an “extraordinary circumstance” that is out of the airline’s control, Lukacs says. Air Canada says it cancelled about 250 flights, affecting some 27,000 passengers after the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration issued the ground stop order on Friday, halting all U.S. flights for more than four hours. Meanwhile, Porter Airlines and WestJet say it will likely take the whole weekend for flights to return to normal schedules. Lukacs notes that travellers flying between Canada and the U.S. are protected under both countries’ air passenger regulations, but Canada’s protections are stronger. For Canadians stuck in the U.S. who may have had to book hotels and cover the cost of additional meals because of travel delays, Lukacs says airlines are not required to pay travellers back. “In Europe, passengers would still be getting meals and accommodation,” Lukacs says, even for disruptions outside the airline’s control. “In Canada, that’s not an obligation.” Lukacs says if Canadians feel airlines have not met their obligations under the law, they should document their communications with the airline and take them to small claims court. The U.S. government says the ground stop order was issued on Friday after new technology was added to the nation’s air traffic control system, overloading antiquated equipment and causing intermittent communications and radar gaps. The matter is under investigation. This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 14, 2026. Kathryn Mannie, The Canadian Press

DUBLIN, Nov 14 : Ireland secured an emphatic 43-15 victory over Fiji in the Nations Championship on Saturday to stay in contention for a place in the final of the new competition.
Ireland were 17-15 ahead at halftime and stretched their lead after the break to move to 20 points in the Northern Hemisphere standings, level with England and a point behind France.
Wingers Tommy O’Brien and Robert Baloucoune scored two tries each with Ronan Kelleher, Andrew Porter and Nick Tominey getting the other three.
Fiji’s two tries came with four minutes midway through the first half from Josua Tuisova and captain Peceli Yato.

Ireland were wary of the danger of another upset in the Nations Championship after New Zealand and South Africa were beaten this weekend, but O’Brien went over in the eighth minute to settle their nerves.
Fiji’s double strike put them 12-7 ahead, however, before right wing Baloucoune went over twice in the last 10 minutes of the first half.
Ben Volavola’s penalty on the stroke of halftime reduced Ireland’s lead to two points but after the interval the gulf in quality became more apparent.
Ireland stretched their lead when Kelleher scored from a lineout maul and Porter placed the ball over the line from a simple tap-and-go.
Fiji’s desperation to stay in the contest led to many mistakes and Ireland took advantage in the 59th minute as Sam Prendergast sent a superb grubber kick through for O’Brien to pounce on before Timoney completed the rout.
Ireland must now beat South Africa and hope France, who host Argentina, and England, who take on New Zealand, falter in Saturday’s matches to secure a place in the final at Twickenham on November 29.
(Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by Ed Osmond)

FAST

BRAGA, Portugal, Nov 14 : Portugal's first match since Cristiano Ronaldo's international retirement ended in a crushing 4-1 home defeat by Denmark in the Nations League on Saturday, with Rasmus Hojlund scoring twice as a night of tributes in Braga turned sour for Jorge Jesus and his players.
Norway beat Wales 3-1 in Oslo in the other League A Group Four match, with Antonio Nusa and Andreas Schjelderup scoring before Erling Haaland's late penalty sealed victory.
Portugal remain top on 12 points, three ahead of Denmark, with Norway third on six and Wales bottom on three. One round of league-phase matches remains, with Wales hosting Portugal and Denmark at home to Norway on Tuesday.
In front of a packed stadium, Portugal's players wore shirts bearing Ronaldo's name and number seven during the national anthem.

Supporters unfurled a banner reading "Obrigado, capi7ão" — "Thank you, captain" — alongside images of him lifting the European Championship and Nations League trophies.
Ronaldo announced his international retirement on social media last week following a public falling-out with manager Jesus.
DENMARK RUN RIOT
Portugal dominated much of the first half in pouring rain but fell behind shortly before halftime.
Hojlund had a header ruled out for a foul by Joachim Andersen in the build-up before another aerial effort struck Ruben Dias’ hand. Following a VAR intervention and pitchside review, the referee awarded a penalty which Denmark captain Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg drove into the top-right corner shortly before halftime.
Hojlund doubled Denmark's advantage five minutes after the interval, slipping behind the defence to meet a cross from the right with a powerful volley.
The striker scored again seven minutes later, cutting inside Renato Veiga on a counter-attack before firing a right-footed shot past Diogo Costa from the edge of the box.
Andersen completed the rout in the 75th minute, rising to power home a towering header from i.nside the area after Mathias Jensen delivered a free kick from the right.
Bernardo Silva scored a consolation goal for Portugal three minutes into added time, firing home from close range after the goalkeeper parried the ball.
“Practically everything went wrong for us... It’s actually hard to find an explanation," midfielder Joao Palhinha told Portuguese broadcaster Sport TV. 
"It was an unlucky night for us; we made it far too easy for our opponents. We’ve got a match on Tuesday, so we’ve got until then to reflect about what happened today. But I have no doubt whatsoever that we’ll bounce back and secure top spot in the group in Wales.”
NORWAY PUNISH WALES
After a subdued first half at Ullevaal Stadion, Nusa broke the deadlock in the 59th minute with a half-volley from the edge of the area following a partially cleared corner.
Schjelderup doubled the lead two minutes after coming off the bench. Nusa raced down the left and fed Haaland, who squared for the substitute to tap into an empty net at the far post.
David Brooks gave Wales hope in the 79th minute, racing onto a through ball and chipping the advancing goalkeeper despite pressure from a defender.
But Connor Roberts fouled Schjelderup inside the area six minutes later and Haaland converted the resulting penalty in the 88th minute to secure Norway's win.

Source: Reuters

INDIAN WELLS, California, Nov 14 : Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva extended her unbeaten run at the WTA Finals on Saturday, dispatching American Jessica Pegula 6-3 6-4 to reach the final, where she will face a resurgent Elina Svitolina.
Andreeva's heavy groundstrokes, strong serving and tireless defense were too much for the American in their first career meeting, played under sunny skies in the California desert.
"It was a tough match," Andreeva said. "You have to work hard to win a point against her. She is going to leave everything out there and make your life complicated, so I wanted to make her life complicated as well today."
The opening set was tight until Andreeva pounced on a looping shot from Pegula and drilled a forehand winner to break serve for a 5-3 lead.

Pegula, backed by a supportive crowd, earned break points as Andreeva served for the set, but shanked an overhead and Andreeva took the set two points later when her opponent's backhand found the net.
Pegula broke to grab a 3-1 advantage in the second set but the lead would prove short-lived. Andreeva broke straight back with a deft volley and broke again to lead 4-3. The tournament's third seed ultimately sealed the win when a Pegula backhand sailed long on match point.
Andreeva, making her WTA Finals debut, has not dropped a set in four matches at the event.
SVITOLINA SHINES
She will face sixth seed Elina Svitolina in Sunday's final after the Ukrainian needed just over an hour to cruise past Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova 6-2 6-1 in Saturday's other semi-final.
Despite strong sun shining in her eyes, Svitolina delivered a crosscourt backhand winner to claim the first set.
She raced out to a 5-0 lead in the second and raised her arms in triumph and beamed a smile after Noskova's forehand went wide on match point.
Andreeva holds a 2-1 lead in their head-to-head matchups, including a one-sided 6-4 6-0 victory in their round-robin match on Monday, but Svitolina has raised her level since.
"It's going to be another big challenge, of course, and I feel I have to do my homework," she said.
"But I feel I'm a completely different player from the first match. I was not playing the right way. I will give it my best shot."
Svitolina has now made the final all three times she has competed in the eight-player championships, winning it in 2018.
The $10 million tournament was moved from Riyadh to the Indian Wells Tennis Garden because of the US-Israeli war with Iran.

items.author: Enda Curran
items.summary: Los responsables de la Fed subieron las tasas un cuarto de punto en septiembre, hasta un rango objetivo del 3,75% al 4%, y luego las mantuvieron sin cambios en la reunión del FOMC celebrada en octubre ...
items.body: Bloomberg — El debate sobre la política monetaria de EE.UU. ya se ha trasladado a enero. En una serie de discursos y entrevistas esta semana, los funcionarios de la Reserva Federal consolidaron las expectativas del mercado respecto a una subida de las tasas de interés en diciembre y abrieron la posibilidad de los primeros aumentos consecutivos desde 2023. El martes cobró mayor urgencia la necesidad de aumentar las tasas de interés, cuando el informe de precios al consumidor de octubre mostró que la inflación se aceleró y se extendió a todos los bienes y servicios cotidianos. Ver más: ¿Qué señales de alerta deja el último dato de inflación de EE.UU. para la Fed? “La inflación es demasiado alta”, dijo el presidente de la Reserva Federal de Nueva York, John Williams, mientras que Austan Goolsbee, de la Reserva Federal de Chicago, describió los datos como “casi preocupantes”. La presidenta de la Reserva Federal de Dallas, Lorie Logan, dijo que los funcionarios podrían tener que subir las tasas “más rápidamente” de lo que esperaba, mientras que el gobernador de la Reserva Federal, Christopher Waller, llegó incluso a advertir que podría ser necesario un aumento de 50 puntos básicos el próximo mes. “Diciembre está claramente preparado para un alza de tasas de 25 puntos básicos”, afirmó Olu Sonola, jefe de economía estadounidense de Fitch Ratings. “Las verdaderas incógnitas son con qué rapidez se producirá la siguiente subida y cuántas más serán necesarias en última instancia”. Aproximadamente la mitad de los 19 miembros del Comité Federal de Mercado Abierto, y aproximadamente la mitad de quienes votarán en las reuniones de diciembre y enero, se han pronunciado a lo largo de la semana. En cuanto a las dos últimas cuestiones, las señales han sido contradictorias. Estas oscilaron desde la referencia de Waller a un aumento de gran envergadura hasta la reiteración por parte de Beth Hammack, de la Fed de Cleveland, de su preferencia por subidas más frecuentes y de menor magnitud, pasando por la postura de la presidenta de la Fed de Filadelfia, Anna Paulson, a favor de un ritmo gradual en los incrementos. Ver más: Citi prevé más alzas de tasas de la Fed, pero no espera un dólar más fuerte: las razones El viernes se conocieron más malas noticias cuando los datos revelaron que los precios al por mayor —que alimentan el indicador de inflación preferido por la Fed— subieron en octubre con respecto al año anterior a su ritmo más rápido desde 2022. Los costos de transporte y almacenamiento se dispararon, lo que se sumó a las pruebas de presiones persistentes sobre los precios en toda la economía. “Ahora parece que existe preocupación por adelantarse a la nueva aceleración, aumentar la frecuencia y, potencialmente, incrementar lo que el FOMC considera terminal”, es decir, hasta qué punto deberían subir las tasas de interés, dijo Michael Reid, jefe de economía estadounidense del Royal Bank of Canada. Los economistas de Bank of America ( BAC ) y de Santander US Capital Markets han aumentado el número de alzas que prevén tras la semana de datos y la avalancha de discursos. Bank of America prevé ahora subidas en las tres próximas reuniones de la Fed, mientras que Santander prevé dos aumentos, en diciembre y marzo. Los argumentos a favor de la cautela se basan en sectores de la economía vulnerables al aumento de los costos de financiación, como el mercado inmobiliario. Los datos económicos de esta semana pusieron de manifiesto lo deprimido que se encuentra ese sector, con las ventas de viviendas de segunda mano cayendo el mes pasado a su nivel más bajo en 16 años. La presidenta de la Fed de Boston, Susan Collins, reconoció el viernes que unas tasas de interés más altas pueden afectar a la asequibilidad de la vivienda, pero añadió que la estabilidad de los precios, a largo plazo, es más importante para el sector inmobiliario y para la economía en su conjunto. Ver más: Waller, de la Fed, abre la puerta a una posible subida de tasas de medio punto en diciembre “Me parece que la dirección adecuada para la política monetaria es clara”, dijo, refiriéndose a la necesidad de subir las tasas de interés. Sin embargo, en una entrevista con Bloomberg Television , no reveló cuál creía que sería el ritmo correcto. “No quiero adelantarme en cuanto a hasta dónde deberíamos llegar o a qué velocidad”, dijo. La volatilidad del mercado bursátil, vinculada a las preocupaciones sobre una desaceleración del auge de la inteligencia artificial, constituye otro motivo de inquietud. La gobernadora de la Reserva Federal, Michelle Bowman, advirtió de los riesgos, entre los que se incluye una fuerte caída de los precios de las acciones si la rentabilidad de las inversiones en IA no cumple con las expectativas. “La reducción de los precios de las acciones podría debilitar la capacidad de respuesta del gasto de los consumidores”, afirmó. “Y el aumento de las tasas de interés podría ejercer aún más presión sobre sectores de la economía sensibles a las fluctuaciones, como el sector inmobiliario y la inversión en pequeñas empresas”. Otra variable es la posibilidad de que los precios de la energía bajen en los próximos meses, lo que aliviaría la presión sobre los costos de los combustibles y supondría un respiro para los hogares y las empresas. El presidente de la Fed de Richmond, Tom Barkin, quien intervino el lunes, señaló que las tasas deben subir, pero a un ritmo prudente. “La mayoría de los funcionarios de la Reserva Federal parecen estar de acuerdo en la necesidad de subir las tasas de interés y en la preferencia por no precipitarse”, afirmó Eric Wallerstein, jefe de estrategia macroeconómica de Clocktower Group y anteriormente asesor del exgobernador de la Reserva Federal, Stephen Miran. Los responsables de la Fed subieron las tasas un cuarto de punto en septiembre, hasta un rango objetivo del 3,75% al 4%, y luego las mantuvieron sin cambios en la última reunión del FOMC celebrada en octubre. Ver más: Daly, de la Fed, dice que probablemente se necesiten más alzas de tasas para contener los precios El presidente de la Fed, Kevin Warsh, que no se ha pronunciado públicamente desde su rueda de prensa de octubre, tiene previsto hablar sobre su grupo de trabajo sobre inteligencia artificial y productividad en un acto que se celebrará el lunes. Pocos esperan que se desvíe de su preferencia declarada de no ofrecer ninguna orientación sobre las perspectivas a corto plazo de la política monetaria. Sin embargo, los inversores no están esperando y ya han descontado aumentos de un cuarto de punto para diciembre, enero y marzo. Antes de esta semana, los inversores habían anticipado incrementos en diciembre y marzo. Como ejemplo de la sacudida que supuso para los mercados la comunicación de la Fed de esta semana, los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro se dispararon tras las declaraciones de Waller y Logan, quienes intervinieron antes y después de que se publicaran el martes los datos de inflación, más elevados de lo esperado. El rendimiento de los bonos a dos años subió 19 puntos básicos hasta el 4,75% ese mismo día, su mayor alza desde que los anuncios arancelarios del presidente Donald Trump agitaran los mercados mundiales en abril de 2025. “Las directrices de la Reserva Federal son un tanto confusas y han provocado grandes fluctuaciones en los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro, y una vez más, dado que el presidente Warsh se abstiene de hacer comentarios, otros están llenando el vacío”, dijo la economista jefe de Nationwide, Kathy Bostjancic. En última instancia, la aceleración del crecimiento económico podría servir de pretexto a la Fed para subir las tasas. Los datos de la semana pasada mostraron que el empleo creció con fuerza en octubre y que la tasa de desempleo descendió ligeramente. Los responsables recibirán un informe más sobre el empleo y otra lectura de la inflación de octubre antes de reunirse de nuevo en diciembre. Pocos observadores esperan que ese conjunto de datos revele una desaceleración significativa. “El gradualismo es un error de política económica en una economía con fuerte crecimiento y alta inflación”, afirmó Robert Sockin, economista jefe para Estados Unidos de PGIM. “La historia sugiere que existe un alto riesgo de que este enfoque, en última instancia, lleve a un banco central a tener que endurecer su política monetaria más rápidamente y en mayor medida de lo que habría tenido que hacerlo de otro modo”. items.title: La tecnología del siglo XIX que Nvidia quiere cambiar para impulsar los centros de datos de IA
items.author: Emily Forgash, Michelle Ma, Mark Chediak
items.summary: La influencia de Nvidia ha impulsado una carrera para fabricar nuevos transformadores de potencia que sean más eficientes, que puedan gestionar mejor las amplias fluctuaciones de la demanda de centros ...
items.body: Bloomberg — La expansión de los centros de datos que sustentan la inteligencia artificial depende de un equipo cuya tecnología apenas ha evolucionado desde el siglo XIX. Sin embargo, eso podría estar a punto de cambiar. La influencia del gigante de los chips Nvidia Corp. ( NVDA ) ha impulsado una carrera para fabricar nuevos transformadores de potencia que sean más eficientes, que puedan gestionar mejor las amplias fluctuaciones de la demanda de los centros de datos y, lo que es fundamental, que ahorren espacio en las instalaciones para la capacidad de procesamiento. Ver más: Polémica de Jensen Huang opaca anuncio de alianzas de Nvidia con empresas de IA de Corea del Sur Para el empresario del sector de la energía solar Meir Adest, el plan de Nvidia supuso un momento de inspiración. Vio un mercado viable para un novedoso dispositivo eléctrico que su empresa, SolarEdge Technologies Inc., había comenzado a desarrollar en su momento, pero que abandonó durante una recesión del mercado. “Ya llevábamos años perfeccionando” una tecnología que eliminaría la necesidad de los transformadores tradicionales, afirmó Adest, cofundador de SolarEdge, en una entrevista. “Parecía el paso lógico” modificar sus prototipos para adaptarlos a la visión de Nvidia. El auge de los centros de datos está generando un gasto de capital de billones de dólares, y la prisa por ponerlos en funcionamiento se ve limitada sobre todo por el acceso a la red eléctrica. Las empresas de suministro eléctrico tienen dificultades para conectar las instalaciones previstas, lo que está provocando un aumento fuerte de los precios en algunas zonas de EE.UU. y generando una intensa reacción negativa, lo que, en parte, ha impulsado la victoria arrolladora de los demócratas en las elecciones de mitad de legislatura. Los demócratas victoriosos en una amplia franja de estados han prometido poner freno a la expansión de los centros de datos, especialmente en Texas, donde se está construyendo más de una cuarta parte de los centros de datos de EE.UU. Esto significa que la eficiencia energética y el aprovechamiento máximo de la infraestructura ya autorizada serán fundamentales para los constructores. Los nuevos dispositivos, conocidos como transformadores de estado sólido, ofrecen una solución para aliviar la presión sobre la red eléctrica —y podrían suponer una lucrativa oportunidad para las empresas que sean las primeras en comercializarlos. Ver más: ¿Qué negocios y conexiones en China tiene Alice Huang, señalada en la polémica del CEO de Nvidia? Los transformadores convencionales, utilizados comercialmente por primera vez a finales del siglo XIX, emplean bobinas, magnetismo y metal para convertir los niveles de voltaje. Estos equipos reducen los altos voltajes que transportan las redes eléctricas a niveles que pueden utilizarse en las instalaciones, y viceversa. Debido a la enorme cantidad de energía que necesita un centro de datos, estos equipos pueden ocupar una parte considerable de sus instalaciones. El año pasado, Nvidia instó al sector de los centros de datos a plantearse el cambio a una fuente de alimentación de corriente continua en lugar de la corriente alterna que prevalece en la actualidad. Ahí es donde entran en juego los transformadores de estado sólido. Constituyen un intento de utilizar electrónica de potencia y semiconductores para suministrar energía de corriente continua a los racks informáticos, al tiempo que se eliminan las etapas de conversión de potencia, lo que en su conjunto limita la pérdida de energía. Aunque los transformadores de estado sólido ya se han utilizado para mejorar la recarga de vehículos eléctricos, esta tecnología se encuentra, en el mejor de los casos, a un año de su comercialización para los centros de datos de EE.UU. En primer lugar, deben ser capaces de gestionar tensiones mucho más elevadas, grandes variaciones en la demanda y cumplir con los estándares de fiabilidad que requieren los centros de datos. Además, su fabricación e instalación resultan más costosas que las de los transformadores tradicionales. No obstante, estos retos no han frenado el entusiasmo por lo que pronto podría convertirse en una infraestructura fundamental de los futuros centros de datos. Una vez que los transformadores de estado sólido estén disponibles comercialmente, los analistas de Jefferies, liderados por Julien Dumoulin-Smith, predicen que el mercado estadounidense alcanzará los US$4.300 millones anuales para 2030. Las empresas que desarrollan los nuevos transformadores apuestan por que los operadores de centros de datos recurrirán a esta tecnología a largo plazo, ya que les permitirá liberar más espacio para los procesadores informáticos de IA, al tiempo que reducen los costos de los equipos. BloombergNEF estima que el ahorro ascenderá a US$1,39 millones por cada megavatio de demanda eléctrica de los centros de datos. (Algunos centros de datos propuestos superan los 1.000 megavatios, lo que equivale a la capacidad de un reactor nuclear tradicional). Los transformadores de estado sólido “convierten lo que históricamente ha sido un equipo pasivo en una infraestructura controlable, lo cual, dada la dinámica y la presión a la que está sometida la red eléctrica, es realmente importante”, dijo Victoria Beasley, socia fundadora de Gigascale Capital y patrocinadora de la empresa emergente Heron Power Electronics Co. Ver más: ¿Quién es Alice Huang, la presunta espía de Jensen Huang, CEO de Nvidia? El grupo chino Envision Group anunció la semana pasada que había logrado la primera implantación comercial a nivel mundial de un sistema para centros de datos que utiliza un transformador de estado sólido en su campus de Ulanqab, y las empresas estadounidenses se apresuran a ponerse al día. Las empresas solares que cotizan en bolsa, Enphase Energy Inc. y SolarEdge, han detectado la oportunidad de aprovechar su experiencia en electrónica de potencia y tecnología de corriente continua ante la ralentización del crecimiento de las ventas de sistemas solares residenciales. SolarEdge afirma que está probando un prototipo, mientras que Enphase realizó con éxito una demostración de su propio dispositivo a finales de octubre. Ambas empresas esperan realizar pruebas piloto de sus dispositivos el próximo año y comenzar los envíos comerciales en 2028. El CEO de Enphase, Badri Kothandaraman, dijo en una conferencia telefónica sobre los resultados del tercer trimestre que los dispositivos tienen “el potencial de convertirse en un negocio de ingresos anuales de mil millones de dólares” para la compañía solo en el mercado de centros de datos. Raghu Belur, director de productos de Enphase, calificó los nuevos transformadores como una medida “obvia” para los centros de datos, ya que permitirían ahorrar en la compra de energía de la red. “Para un centro de datos de un gigavatio, si se logra una eficiencia un 5% mayor, eso representa un ahorro de US$30 millones solo en costos de energía”, afirmó durante una reciente presentación sobre el transformador de estado sólido de la compañía en una conferencia de IA en Santa Clara, California. GE Vernova Inc., uno de los mayores fabricantes mundiales de equipos eléctricos, tiene previsto probar un transformador de estado sólido de 5 megavatios con un cliente a finales de este año, según declaró en verano su CEO, Scott Strazik. No obstante, señaló que los primeros pedidos no llegarán antes de 2027. El lanzamiento dependerá de la rapidez con la que los centros de datos adopten la corriente continua, señaló. Las empresas emergentes también están realizando sus propios intentos para desarrollar esta tecnología. Dos de ellas están dirigidas por antiguos empleados de Tesla Inc. ( TSLA ): Heron Power anunció en agosto que se encontraba en la fase de preproducción, antes de que se esperen sus primeras unidades de producción en serie en la segunda mitad de 2027, mientras que Amperesand Pte. declaró ese mismo mes que había puesto en marcha una línea de producción. DG Matrix Inc. está más avanzada en su desarrollo, con proyecciones de enviar hasta 2.000 transformadores en 2027, según declaró su CEO, Haroon Inam, en una entrevista. Axios informó el mes pasado que la compañía planea recaudar US$250 millones en una ronda de financiación Serie B el próximo año. DG Matrix ha pasado del sector de la carga de vehículos eléctricos, que requiere voltajes más bajos, al desarrollo de tecnología para centros de datos. Inam explicó que la tecnología de su empresa incluye múltiples “puertos” que permiten varias entradas y salidas de electricidad simultáneamente. Ver más: Acciones de Nvidia caen tras investigación de la junta directiva a su CEO, Jensen Huang, por una infidelidad Dumoulin-Smith predice que la dependencia de estas empresas de la nueva tecnología para generar ingresos variará según su tamaño. Para GE Vernova, se espera que los transformadores de estado sólido representen una parte mínima de sus ingresos, mientras que para Enphase y SolarEdge, estos dispositivos podrían alcanzar el 15% y el 11% de los ingresos de la compañía para 2030, respectivamente. Para validar sus proyectos a corto plazo, las empresas de energía solar deberán anunciar un programa piloto con un proveedor de servicios en la nube de gran tamaño, afirmó. Brian Dow, CEO de Ampersand, cree que, con el tiempo, una sola empresa acaparará entre el 30% y el 40% del mercado, y el sector, cada vez más saturado, irá eliminando a los pocos ganadores. Ninguna de estas innovaciones se estaría produciendo a tan gran escala sin el atractivo de las grandes empresas tecnológicas y su enorme poder adquisitivo, afirmó Caitilín McManus, analista de BNEF. “Ahora, con el capital adicional disponible gracias a los centros de datos, se está dando un impulso aún mayor”. FAST

STARBASE, Texas: SpaceX's Starship spacecraft on Saturday (Nov 14) returned from a 22-hour voyage in orbit and descended for the first time into the grasp of giant mechanical arms at the Texas tower it was launched from a day earlier, a catch that is essential to the company's decade-long effort to develop a fully reusable rocket.

The 171-foot-tall Starship fell out of thick clouds over SpaceX's Starbase launch site, reignited engines to flip itself vertical and slowly descended into the tower's "Mechazilla" arms, engines still roaring. Charred from the blazing heat of its return from space, the ship shut down its engines and hung still after the rocket system's longest mission yet.
The towering two-stage rocket's Super Heavy booster — the rocket's bottom half — carried Starship to space on Friday, lifting off from SpaceX's Starbase, Texas, facilities. That booster had failed to make a similar return to the launch pad some 10 minutes after liftoff, nixing SpaceX's plan to recover both parts of the rocket for the first time.
But the Starship upper stage's successful return after orbiting Earth 14 times for over 22 hours marked a key engineering milestone in the whirlwind, multibillion-dollar development of Starship, which billionaire Elon Musk sees as the future workhorse for SpaceX's lucrative Starlink satellite business, as well as ambitions to put data centres in orbit, return humans to the moon and, eventually, settle on Mars.
After deploying 26 Starlink satellites in orbit Friday night while cruising some 161 miles (260km) in altitude, Starship on Saturday fired one of its engines to begin an atmospheric plunge. It faced blistering heat as its orbital speed of some 17,000 miles per hour slowed to a supersonic free-fall in the skies above SpaceX's Starbase facilities on the Gulf coast of south Texas.

The spacecraft then reignited three engines to flip itself in a vertical position and steer itself toward the launch tower, where two mechanical "chopstick" arms clasped onto the spacecraft as it hovered in place.
SpaceX's dominance in the global launch industry is centred on its workhorse Falcon 9 rocket, which has launched over 700 times since 2010. That rocket's first stage is reusable, but its second stage - the part that delivers payloads into orbit - is discarded into the ocean after each flight.
With Starship, Musk wants a rocket system that can fly to space and back in a manner and tempo akin to commercial airplanes.
Though Saturday's Starship recovery is a key milestone in that effort, SpaceX has yet to recover both Starship stages in a single mission. And Starship's heat-shield, composed of black hexagonal tiles that protect it from the blazing heat of atmospheric reentry, is itself not yet fully reusable.
SpaceX is trying to engineer new tile designs that will require little to no refurbishment after each mission.
NASA's Space Shuttle system that ferried astronauts to the International Space Station before its 2011 retirement was partially reusable; its booster stages that got it off Earth were discarded after each flight. The reusable spacecraft itself had to go through extensive refurbishment before re-flying.

Source: Reuters/rj

STARBASE, Texas: SpaceX's Starship spacecraft on Saturday (Nov 14) returned from a 22-hour voyage in orbit and descended for the first time into the grasp of giant mechanical arms at the Texas tower it was launched from a day earlier, a catch that is essential to the company's decade-long effort to develop a fully reusable rocket.

The 171-foot-tall Starship fell out of thick clouds over SpaceX's Starbase launch site, reignited engines to flip itself vertical and slowly descended into the tower's "Mechazilla" arms, engines still roaring. Charred from the blazing heat of its return from space, the ship shut down its engines and hung still after the rocket system's longest mission yet.
The towering two-stage rocket's Super Heavy booster — the rocket's bottom half — carried Starship to space on Friday, lifting off from SpaceX's Starbase, Texas, facilities. That booster had failed to make a similar return to the launch pad some 10 minutes after liftoff, nixing SpaceX's plan to recover both parts of the rocket for the first time.
But the Starship upper stage's successful return after orbiting Earth 14 times for over 22 hours marked a key engineering milestone in the whirlwind, multibillion-dollar development of Starship, which billionaire Elon Musk sees as the future workhorse for SpaceX's lucrative Starlink satellite business, as well as ambitions to put data centres in orbit, return humans to the moon and, eventually, settle on Mars.
After deploying 26 Starlink satellites in orbit Friday night while cruising some 161 miles (260km) in altitude, Starship on Saturday fired one of its engines to begin an atmospheric plunge. It faced blistering heat as its orbital speed of some 17,000 miles per hour slowed to a supersonic free-fall in the skies above SpaceX's Starbase facilities on the Gulf coast of south Texas.

Nov 14 (Reuters) – State and federal officers on Saturday searched a biofuels plant in Peoria, Illinois, for explosives after a device deemed a “credible threat” was found nearby, officials said, prompting a notice for residents to evacuate an area with a 1-mile radius.

The evacuation order was lifted on Saturday, almost a full day after the device was discovered on Friday close to the BioUrja ethanol plant in Peoria, a city of about 110,000 people, some 150 miles (240 km) southwest of Chicago, officials said. Bomb technicians rendered it safe, Peoria police said. 

Law enforcement personnel on Saturday afternoon finished their search of the sprawling facility, which is the size of 44-1/2 football fields, Peoria Police Chief Brad Dixon said.

Show Full Article

A standard American football field occupies roughly 1.3 acres (0.5 hectares).  

The Peoria Police Department said in a statement on Facebook that nothing “of concern” was found and the evacuation notice was lifted.

The owner of the plant, the BioUrja Group of Houston, Texas, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The incident began on Friday after the plant informed the police that it had received a bomb threat. Dixon on Saturday said he would not call the device a bomb because the process for determining its composition was ongoing. 

“I can just tell you it was deemed a credible threat,” Dixon told reporters at a briefing. “There’s an extensive criminal investigation going on.”

Officials determined a potential blast radius of 1 mile based not solely on the device itself, but also on the materials nearby, Dixon said.

Officials from the FBI and the US Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives told reporters that their personnel, including explosives experts, were helping to search the facility and were aiding in the hunt for whoever was responsible for the device.

(Reporting by Jonathan Landay and Ismail Shakil; Editing by Sergio Non and Franklin Paul)

Fed's Collins says gradual rate hikes best to manage economic risks

A number of Fed officials have said a more measured pace of rate increases allows the economy time to adjust to the rise in borrowing costs.

In this Feb 5, 2018, file photo, the seal of the Board of Governors of the United States Federal Reserve System is displayed in the ground at the Marriner S Eccles Federal Reserve Board Building in Washington. Susan Collins, the new president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston, said Sep 26 2022, that a higher unemployment will be needed to bring down inflation from unusually high levels, but suggested any economic downturn would be modest. FAST

BOSTON: Fed eral Reserve Bank of Boston President Susan Collins said on Saturday (Nov 14) she supported a steady pace of modest interest rate increases because that path of action better managed economic uncertainties.
When it comes to moving monetary policy to a tighter footing, "a steady, gradual path seems appropriate to me at the moment. But I'm open-minded," Collins told reporters at a conference held by her bank on housing issues in Boston.
“I do see the risks as two-sided on the real side of the economy," Collins said, with inflation high and its gains broadening throughout the economy, while the job market was stable with the potential to accelerate.
At the same time, there are the ongoing risks of more shocks hitting the economy, Collins said. Furthermore, “it's possible that the rise in medium to longer term rates that we've seen since the beginning of the year may actually weigh on demand more than I'm thinking,” and serve as another source of restraint on economic activity, she said.

For now, all of that argues against the Fed shifting to a more aggressive pace of rate rises to contain inflation that has overshot the Fed ’s 2 per cent target for more than five years, Collins said.

RATE INCREASES IN DECEMBER, JANUARY SEEN The Fed last raised rates in September, and it is widely expected to lift its current 3.75 per cent to 4 per cent interest rate target range by a quarter percentage point at the December 8-9 monetary policy meeting, following that with another increase in January.
Most Fed officials have signalled support for steady and small increases to help lower inflation, but last week's price data and the comments of Fed Governor Christopher Waller have suggested some on the Fed may want a bigger increase next month.
A number of Fed officials have said a more measured pace of rate increases allows the economy time to adjust to the rise in borrowing costs.
Collins cautioned that her expectation that the Fed can move gradually "doesn't necessarily mean a particular cadence." She also reiterated that the data flow from recent months has shifted where the Fed could end up in its current tightening cycle.
“I do think that the price data we've seen over the past three months, and the labor market on a stronger footing, does make me think that the path of policy rates over the, you know, next year might be a bit higher than I had thought a couple of months ago,” Collins said.

MADRID, Nov 14 : England manager Thomas Tuchel does not expect racist abuse during Sunday's Nations League clash with Spain but said his players would be reminded of anti-racism protocols, prompting a terse response from Spain coach Luis de la Fuente.
England face the world champions in Madrid with top spot in their Nations League group at stake, returning to the Spanish capital for the first time since a 2004 friendly in which Black England players, including Ashley Cole and Shaun Wright-Phillips, were subjected to racist abuse from the crowd.
England midfielder Declan Rice said the squad knew exactly how to respond if racism occurred.
"In the past, I've experienced that in Montenegro, Bulgaria and there was a protocol in place we followed," Rice told reporters on Saturday. "We came off the pitch. We know exactly where we are as a group on that.

"I'm not expecting any of that. This is a beautiful city, great stadium, the players we're playing against we have a lot of respect for. It's set up to be a really good evening and hopefully not a negative one."
The issue gained traction after Spain were fined $20,000 following anti-Muslim chants by supporters during a match against Egypt in Barcelona in March.
Spain must also play their next home friendly with a reduced-capacity crowd as part of the punishment.
RACISM NOT A PROBLEM IN SPAIN
De la Fuente rejected any suggestion that racism was a problem in Spain.
"What I can tell you, and you can pass this on to Thomas, is that there is no racism in Spain. That's how strongly I feel about it," De la Fuente said.
"There is no racism. Just as in England, there is no racism in Spain. None of us are racist."
Tuchel bristled when told of De la Fuente's remarks, accusing sections of the Spanish media of misrepresenting his comments.
"I was polite enough to (answer) a question from your colleagues, and you run and ask the other coach and tell him that I talk about racism in Spain," Tuchel said.
"I never talked about racism in Spain. I answered politely a question about what happens. I never expect racism and the dressing room is the most anti-racist place on earth."
James Trafford will start in goal for England on Saturday, said Tuchel, who added that everyone was fit to play including Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence who have recovered from injury.

items.title: EE.UU. investiga si la contratista L3Harris causó la falla que paralizó los vuelos en todo el país
items.author: Cam Kettles, Aidan Williams
items.summary: La paralización de vuelos del viernes fue la suspensión de vuelos más prolongada a nivel nacional desde los atentados terroristas del 11 de septiembre de 2001.
items.body: Bloomberg — El secretario de Transporte, Sean Duffy, declaró el sábado que las autoridades están investigando si la empresa contratista aeroespacial y de defensa L3Harris Technologies Inc. tuvo la culpa de la interrupción del sistema de control de tráfico aéreo que dejó en tierra los vuelos en todo el país durante más de cuatro horas. L3Harris estaba reemplazando una línea de cobre por fibra óptica en una instalación remota de la Administración Federal de Aviación (FAA) el viernes cuando un enrutador saturó a otros enrutadores con más de 1.000 intentos de conexión cada cuatro o cinco segundos, interrumpiendo las comunicaciones con las aeronaves y algunas señales de radar, explicó Duffy durante una rueda de prensa. Los sistemas volvieron a estar operativos después de que la FAA aislara los trabajos en la instalación, añadió. Ver más: Aerolíneas de EE.UU. intentan normalizar operaciones tras suspensión de vuelos: miles siguen cancelados y retrasados “Por lo tanto, lo que estamos tratando de determinar es si hubo incompetencia”, afirmó Duffy. Planteó la posibilidad de un error de instalación o de un router defectuoso y añadió: “Aún no hemos determinado cuál fue la causa del fallo”. La paralización de vuelos del viernes fue la suspensión de vuelos más prolongada a nivel nacional desde los atentados terroristas del 11 de septiembre de 2001. Bedford indicó que prevé la cancelación de entre 4.000 y 5.000 de los 41.000 vuelos programados para el sábado, debido a la reubicación de aviones y tripulaciones por parte de las aerolíneas. Alrededor de 12.000 vuelos no operaron el viernes, incluyendo aproximadamente 9.000 vuelos comerciales, añadió. Duffy afirmó que las autoridades no creen que el colapso se debiera a un ciberataque. El administrador de la FAA, Bryan Bedford, señaló en la rueda de prensa que no había pruebas de que la inteligencia artificial hubiera intervenido. “Se trató de un sistema de la FAA que no estuvo a la altura de las circunstancias, o bien nuestro contratista no estuvo a la altura, o bien nuestro equipo no estuvo a la altura”, afirmó Duffy, y añadió más tarde que muchos de los contratistas del Gobierno prestan “un servicio realmente deficiente”. AT&T Inc., Verizon Communications Inc. y Lumen Technologies Inc. están colaborando con la FAA en la creación de una red sustitutiva. “Pero, mientras tanto, hasta que pueda construirla, no me queda más remedio que recurrir a L3Harris, propietaria de esta red”, afirmó Duffy. Ver más: EE.UU. levanta suspensión de vuelos tras más de cuatro horas de paralización por una falla técnica L3Harris no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. Sus acciones cerraron el viernes a US$272,35, lo que supone un aumento del 17% respecto al mínimo de las últimas 52 semanas, de US$232,34, registrado el 8 de octubre. Las compañías aéreas esperan restablecer sus horarios completos para el final del domingo, según declaró Bedford a los periodistas. Duffy instó al Congreso a proporcionar US$50.000 millones en fondos de emergencia para modernizar el anticuado sistema de control del tráfico aéreo y señaló que la solicitud se presentará el lunes. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

LONDON, Nov 14 : England winger Will Joseph scored a record-equalling five tries to lead his side to a runaway 78-15 Nations Championship win over Japan at Twickenham on Saturday.
Joseph was making only his second appearance for England, more than four years after his debut, and started his return with a try from his first touch inside the opening 65 seconds before adding three more in the first 25 minutes.
The 24-year-old scored a fifth with an intercept after the interval to equal the record set by Rory Underwood in 1989 and matched by Josh Lewsey in 2003 and Henry Arundell at the last World Cup.
England ran in 13 tries in a record score against Japan, and in the new Nations Championship competition.

There were also scores for Freddie Steward, Ellis Genge, Cadan Murley and Ben Earl in an eight-try spree in the first half and for George Martin, Ben Curry, Marcus Smith and Greg Fisilau after the break.
George Ford converted three tries and kicked a penalty and Henry Slade added two conversions.
Warner Dearns and Helu Opeti claimed Japan’s tries, the first converted by Naoto Saito, who also put over a penalty.
Japan coach Eddie Jones, who spent seven years in charge of England, had promised he would try to create chaos but his game plan was dismantled by England's early try and Japan lock Harry Hockings getting sent to the sin bin for an illegal tackle.
His early yellow card was upgraded to a 20-minute red, and England took full advantage.
"I loved every minute of that and a joy to be part of. It was a pretty perfect day," Joseph said.
There was no let-up as the hosts turned the screws with powerful carrying through the middle, strong rucking and bruising tackling as they moved into second spot in the Northern Hemisphere standings.
"There were a lot of things to be pleased about, with wonderful tries from various sources," England coach Steve Borthwick said.
(Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by Ed Osmond)

Source: Reuters

Ukraine's Zelenskyy escalates criticism of SpaceX over speed caps

The Ukrainian Defence Ministry has raised the issue with SpaceX at the institutional level, Zelenskyy said.

KYIV: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy escalated his criticism of SpaceX on Saturday (Nov 14), saying speed restrictions on its military-grade Starshield satellite terminals had dangerous political implications and undermined critical air defences.
Zelenskyy said Starshield terminals operating in temporarily Russian-occupied territories of Ukraine had been limited to a maximum speed of 161 kph for the past five days, hampering Ukraine's military capabilities.
The Ukrainian Defence Ministry has raised the issue with SpaceX at the institutional level, Zelenskyy said.
"The restrictions have now been in place for five days. They say it is some kind of technical issue. We do not believe that is the case," Zelenskyy told reporters in remarks released by his office on Saturday.

"If you impose restrictions there, you are already partially recognising the temporarily occupied territories as not ours. And that is why I believe we have the right to raise this issue and restore the speed – so that there are no restrictions at all."
Zelenskyy said the speed restrictions made it more difficult for Ukrainian air defence units to intercept Russian jet-powered drones and made Ukrainian cities more vulnerable. He said he had ordered his top military and foreign ministry officials to address the issue and seek clarification.
SpaceX has pushed back against the allegations, denying that it introduced new restrictions or made any changes to its satellite operations.
It is the second such outage in recent weeks. In mid-October, Ukrainian officials said that SpaceX limited the speed of Starlink and its Starshield communication systems to about 160 kph amid tensions with US President Donald Trump's administration over Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries. Service was then restored on Oct 24.

FAST

CARDIFF, Nov 14 : Wales hailed a heroic performance as they scored five tries and defended superbly to beat New Zealand 35-28 on Saturday and end a 73-year wait for a win over the All Blacks.
The shock Nations Championship triumph was a massive fillip for the game in Wales, which had been reeling after a record-breaking run of 18 successive defeats following the last World Cup.
Although they won three of their last five tests, Wales had mustered only five victories in 32 internationals over the last three years.
"The effort that the players and staff have put in over the last 15 months or so, they got what they deserved today. It was an unbelievable performance from the boys," Wales coach Steve Tandy said.

"We spoke about attacking, building the performance and being brave and I thought the boys were, probably over brave before halftime, but they had intent to go after the game.
"When New Zealand were coming back at halftime it would be easy to doubt yourselves, but I thought the last couple of minutes they looked really composed."
Captain Dewi Lake said not having to face up to reporters after another defeat made a pleasant change.
"We got asked a lot of questions last week about performance. We had a lot of tough conversations. It's nothing this group doesn't deserve. Steve talks about performance a lot. That's why when you get it right, the result takes care of itself."
Wales beat Japan 28-21 last weekend in a far from convincing performance.
"I'm always proud of this group. I'm not proud of this group because we've beaten New Zealand. I'm proud of the tough times and the good times they've been through," Lake said.
"Of course, we believed we could do it. Sometimes we can say that and it's a passing comment for people at home. But we meant this."

(Writing by Mark Gleeso; Editing by Ed Osmond)

WASHINGTON: The head of the FAA predicted that US air travel would not return to normal schedules until late Sunday (Nov 15) as the aviation system gradually recovers from a nationwide flight shutdown that officials blamed on routine maintenance gone awry.
As of 4.15pm ET (9.15pm GMT), airlines on Saturday had cancelled more than 5,300 US flights and delayed almost 6,300, according to FlightAware, an aviation website. That followed about 9,200 flights cancelled and 7,500 delayed on Friday after the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop because of disruptions to air traffic communications.
Federal Aviation Administration head Bryan Bedford said on Saturday that he expected airline operations to largely return to normal by late Sunday. He also apologised for the disruption, adding that the system remains stable.
The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop on Friday that halted nearly all departing flights for almost five hours. It was the longest nationwide halt to air travel since the attacks of Sep 11, 2001 and one of the single worst US travel days ever.

The issue prompted the White House to convene an emergency meeting in the Situation Room on Friday and federal agencies to scramble to determine if it was a cyberattack. But the problem was traced to FAA contractor L3Harris' installation of at least one new router at a remote facility, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said on Saturday.
"We're working to determine whether we had incompetence, meaning was it user error or installer error from L3Harris, or did they install a faulty router? We haven't determined what the fault was," Duffy told reporters at a news conference.
L3Harris said it took the issue seriously and is supporting the FAA in its investigation. Its shares last traded down about 4 per cent after hours on Friday.

Related:

FAA begins use of AI tool in bid to reduce flight delays

OVERLOADED COMMUNICATIONS CENTRES Duffy said the trouble began on Friday afternoon, when air traffic control centres experienced instability in radar and communications systems. The router issue led to data overloading other communications centres , officials said.
"We had over 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds, and what that did was (it) gave us issues with our communication with airplanes, and it also caused some disruption with our radar," Duffy added.
The issue affected communications at 17 of the FAA's 22 en route centres , which control aircraft during the cruise portion of a flight. Bedford said the FAA ordered the ground stop in case a centre lost all communications. "No facilities went dark. Nothing was fully lost," Bedford added.
The FAA said it was doing additional testing with L3Harris to see if there are any additional risks.
Delta Air Lines, United Airlines and American Airlines all cancelled about 25 per cent of their flights on Saturday, while JetBlue cancelled nearly 45 per cent . Airlines have issued travel waivers allowing passengers to rebook flights for later dates without cost.
Though the FAA lifted the ground stop on Friday evening, the disruption for passengers was far from over, with tens of thousands of people stranded in airports. Airlines were trying to get flight crews and other personnel in position to resume flights.
The disruption stranded some college football teams on Friday before games scheduled for Saturday.

United States Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy takes questions as US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin looks on in the James S Brady Press Briefing Room at the White House in Washington DC, Nov 13 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Elizabeth Frantz)

FUNDS SOUGHT TO FIX "EMERGENCY" Friday's disruption is the latest and most dramatic sign of strain on a US air traffic control system beset by aging technology, equipment and communications problems and a shortage of several thousand controllers.
Duffy called on Friday for US$50 billion in funding to upgrade air traffic control systems, up from his earlier request of US$30 billion. "This is an emergency," he said.
House Speaker Mike Johnson on Saturday told Fox News that he supports approving more funding for air traffic this year. Johnson's Republicans control Congress until next year, when Democrats will take over because of their gains in the Nov 3 midterm elections.
US Representatives Rick Larsen and Andre Carson, Democrats slated next year to chair the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee and aviation subcommittee, respectively, said in a joint statement Saturday that their panels will "hold the administration accountable for what happened to make sure this chaos does not happen again."
Since receiving $12.5 billion last year, the Transportation Department has awarded contracts worth US$4.3 billion but only spent US$1 billion, Larsen and Carson said.

items.title: Italy fines Meta €805 million over unauthorised access to users' photos
items.author: Bloomberg
items.summary: The authority said it reserves the right to conduct a separate investigation into a new feature launched in 2026 that allows content from users' galleries to be processed in the cloud ...
items.body: The Italian Data Protection Authority fined Meta Platforms Inc. €805 million ($887 million) for accessing photos and videos of Android users’ galleries without their explicit consent. The company accessed photographs, videos and related metadata stored on Italian users’ smartphones through the Facebook app without obtaining consent and without adequately informing them, the Italian regulator said in a statement Saturday. About 20 million Android users are estimated to have been affected. The authority said it reserves the right to conduct a separate investigation into a new feature launched in 2026 that allows content from users’ galleries to be processed in the cloud. Meta didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment. The penalty was imposed on Meta Platforms Ireland Ltd., the company’s main European subsidiary. The size of the fine also takes into consideration a previous 2019 enforcement action against the company, the regulator said. Meta has 60 days to introduce a separate, specific consent request for the feature. The company must also keep the feature disabled by default. The fine is equivalent to about 0.47% of the group’s worldwide revenue, the Italian authority said. (Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

items.title: New to The Street Show #780 Premieres Tonight on Bloomberg Television with Robo.ai, American Fusion, Stewards Investment Capital and FreeCast
items.summary: Jane King hosts conversations on sovereign AI, fusion energy, global private credit and partner-led streaming infrastructure, airing at 6:30 p.m. ET across the United States, Latin America, MENA and ...
items.body:
News
/ ACCESS Newswire
/ New to The Street Show #780 Premieres Tonight on Bloomberg Television with Robo.ai, American Fusion, Stewards Investment Capital and Fr…

New to The Street Show #780 Premieres Tonight on Bloomberg Television with Robo.ai, American Fusion, Stewards Investment Capital and FreeCast 7 min read

AIIO AMFN CAST SWRD
Jane King hosts conversations on sovereign AI, fusion energy, global private credit and partner-led streaming infrastructure, airing at 6:30 p.m. ET across the United States, Latin America, MENA and Southeast Asia
NEW YORK CITY, NY / ACCESS Newswire / November 14, 2026 / AI is driving record spending on data centers, and with it, soaring costs for storage, bandwidth and power. Fusion developers are racing to deliver clean, around-the-clock energy. International investors are looking for returns that don't move with the rest of their portfolios. And companies that already own the customer relationship want to own the screen, too.
Tonight, New to The Street brings leaders working on each of those challenges to a global business audience as Show #780 premieres at 6:30 p.m. ET on Bloomberg Television as sponsored programming, with distribution across the United States, Latin America, the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) and Southeast Asia.
Hosted by Jane King, Show #780 features executive conversations with:
Ralf R. Debbas , President of Robo.ai Inc. AIIO
Dr. Jasem Al Mansoori , Chief Executive Officer of ALIF Holding
Mansoor Ali Khan , Chief Technology Officer of Neurovia AI
Brent Nelson , Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of American Fusion Inc. AMFN
Bilal Adam , Chief Executive Officer of Stewards Investment Capital
William "Bill" Mobley , Founder and Chief Executive Officer of FreeCast, Inc. CAST
"Show #780 is about the infrastructure behind the next economy," said Vince Caruso, Co-Founder and CEO of New to The Street. "A UAE-based, Nasdaq-listed group building sovereign AI and industrial capability. A fusion company opening its technology to independent review. An investment firm connecting emerging and developed markets. And a software company turning every internet connection into a media business. These are the stories our audience in every region tunes in for. No politics. No current events. Only Opportunities To Consider™."
INSIDE SHOW #780
Robo.ai Inc. AIIO : Where Global AI Investment Meets Local Capability
In a three-executive panel, Jane King asks where Robo.ai fits in the AI investment cycle. Ralf R. Debbas, President of Robo.ai, describes the company as a UAE-based, Nasdaq-listed group "connecting regional technology with global market reach."
He outlines its main operating businesses: Neurovia AI, focused on visual data efficiency; ALIF Holding, which brings industrial integration, manufacturing and execution; and Quantum Core Capital (QC Capital), which contributes operating revenue and is developing AI applications including AI-generated video and content creation.
"Our ambition is to help build sovereign AI capabilities within the UAE itself and the wider region," Debbas said, "technology that can be deployed, supported and developed locally."
Dr. Jasem Al Mansoori, Chief Executive Officer of ALIF Holding, Robo.ai's Abu Dhabi-based industrial group, draws on more than 30 years at the UAE Ministry of Interior. "This experience taught me the importance of reliable solutions and strong local support," he said. ALIF is developing an industrial base in the UAE for engineering and manufacturing, and aims to use AI to help industrial customers work more efficiently and make better decisions.
Mansoor Ali Khan, Chief Technology Officer of Neurovia AI, explains why efficiency matters as AI computing competition intensifies and memory and storage costs rise. Khan notes that the large majority of the world's data is visual and unstructured.
Neurovia's flagship NeuroStream™ platform is designed to reduce the volume of visual data that is transmitted, processed and stored. In a company demonstration shown on air, a 12.15 GB 4K video file was reduced to 421 MB, a reduction of more than 96%. Khan said the goal is to address the main costs of AI (storage, compute, transmission and power) and make AI "more affordable and sustainable." Actual results depend on deployment conditions and use-case validation.
Learn more at roboai.group.
American Fusion Inc. AMFN : Independent Review, a New Texas Campus and a Busy Six Months
Chairman and CEO Brent Nelson returns to update Jane King on American Fusion's Texatron™ aneutronic fusion engine. Nelson says an independent third-party reviewer recently completed an on-site evaluation of the technology, with a final report expected later this month. "The draft highlights look good so far," he said, adding that the company hopes the report will confirm "that we're on the right track."
Nelson, who added the CEO title in late October, says his priorities for the next six months include closing on the company's North Texas "Ranch" facility, which American Fusion expects by Thanksgiving, and developing the property. The company is also moving from its temporary facility into new lab and office space, and plans to build its own testing bunker at the Ranch. "We're still operating and testing the Texatron on a daily basis," Nelson said, "and our data is getting better."
He also says the company's patent program remains active, with new applications being written daily, and that its data center proposals are moving forward.
Learn more at americanfusionenergy.com.
Stewards Investment Capital CEO Bilal Adam on Global Investing, Private Credit and Financial Inclusion
Bilal Adam, Chief Executive Officer of Stewards Investment Capital, joins Jane King to discuss the firm's international investment approach, private credit solutions and commitment to financial inclusion. A chartered accountant from South Africa with a background in investment banking, Adam describes building a business with activities spanning South Africa, Mauritius, the United States and Monaco.
Adam discusses the firm's investment philosophy, which he says starts with "aiming to do good first," and its relationship with Nasdaq-listed Stewards, Inc. SWRD , a U.S.-based diversified financial platform led by President and CEO Shaun Quin, which provides financing to small businesses across the United States. Stewards Investment Capital is affiliated with, but separate from, Stewards, Inc. He also highlights telecommunications tower investments aimed at expanding connectivity and financial inclusion in rural African communities.
The conversation explores how Stewards Investment Capital provides pension funds, institutions, family offices and high-net-worth investors with access to private credit, portfolio diversification and international investment opportunities, including a private credit approach that funds fractional amounts of loans to small businesses.
Learn more at stewardsinvestment.com.
FreeCast, Inc. CAST : "The Connection Is Just the Beginning"
Founder and CEO William Mobley explains why FreeCast is "not another streaming service." Instead, the company provides the software infrastructure that lets telecom companies, wireless carriers, internet providers, satellite companies and membership organizations launch their own branded entertainment hubs, offering free television, premium subscriptions, sports, advertising and commerce. "They bring the customers," Mobley said. "We bring the media and monetization technology."
Mobley walks through PEAC, FreeCast's metric for "partner-enabled addressable customers," which measures potential distribution reach through enterprise agreements. He is clear that PEAC does not represent active users, paying subscribers or confirmed revenue. He describes the company's job as converting that reach into activated users, transactions and, ultimately, revenue across advertising, subscriptions, pay-per-view, live sports, rentals and commerce.
"We don't need Netflix to lose for FreeCast to succeed," Mobley said. "We want more content and more services participating in our marketplaces."
Learn more at freecast.com.
FEATURED COMMERCIALS
SafeSpace Global Corporation SSGC : An AI-powered safety and security platform designed to help protect the vulnerable in schools, senior care, addiction treatment, correctional facilities and houses of worship. "Smarter technology, faster response, safer spaces."
T-REX Acquisition Corp. TRXA : Completed a strategic refinancing of its Orofino, Idaho data center and added a new appointment to its board of directors.
Big Sky Industrial BSIN : Advancing helium production, carbon management and strategic energy infrastructure through its flagship Big Sky Carbon Hub, targeting demand from AI, semiconductors, healthcare and aerospace.
Acurx Pharmaceuticals, Inc. ACXP : Developing what could be the first new class of antibiotics in nearly 40 years, with the FDA agreeing to consider a future application for lead drug ibezapolstat based on two planned trials, Pathfinder and Aspire.
HOW TO WATCH
Bloomberg Television: Tonight, Saturday, November 14, 2026, at 6:30 p.m. ET, with distribution across the United States, Latin America, MENA and Southeast Asia
New to The Street TV on YouTube (5.44M+ subscribers): https://www.youtube.com/@NewtoTheStreetTV
NewsOut on YouTube (1.24M+ subscribers): https://www.youtube.com/@NewsOutChannel
Following the broadcast, every segment will be distributed across the New to The Street TV and NewsOut YouTube channels, which together have more than 6.6 million subscribers.
MEET THE COMPANIES 2027: NEW YORK, ATLANTIC CITY AND LAS VEGAS
New to The Street's Meet The Companies tour brings presenting companies face to face with family offices, accredited investors and high-net-worth individuals in three cities in 2027. Every presentation is filmed and distributed across New to The Street's U.S., Latin America, MENA and Southeast Asia platforms and its 6.6M+ subscriber YouTube network, so each company reaches a guaranteed audience well beyond the room. No vendor pitches.
New York - Thursday, January 7, 2027: The Hudson Yards Penthouse, 455 Tenth Avenue PH, New York, NY 10018, the week before the Needham Growth Conference, with a cocktail reception on Wednesday, January 6
Atlantic City - Thursday, January 28, 2027
Las Vegas - June 17-18, 2027
Each event hosts up to 20 presenting companies, with 20-minute slots that include a 15-minute presentation and Q&A. For Atlantic City and Las Vegas presenters, New to The Street pays for your stay.
Confirmed New York Presenters
Glint (glintpay.com)
TMC the metals company Inc. TMC
American Fusion Inc. AMFN
Big Sky Industrial BSIN
T-REX Acquisition Corp. TRXA
Stewards, Inc. SWRD
Roadzen Inc. RDZN
Smile Design Manhattan
Additional presenters will be announced. Accredited investors only. Apply to attend: John@NewtoTheStreet.com. Companies interested in a presenting slot can contact John Battenfield at John@NewtoTheStreet.com.
ABOUT NEW TO THE STREET
Founded in 2009, New to The Street is a sponsored and syndicated business television platform serving public companies, emerging-growth businesses and companies preparing to enter the public markets. Co-founded and led by CEO Vince Caruso, New to The Street combines weekly Bloomberg Television broadcasts across the United States, Latin America, MENA and Southeast Asia with long-form executive interviews, television commercials, earned media, social-media distribution, NewsOut video press-release coverage, accredited-investor events and premium outdoor advertising, including Times Square billboards. The platform has worked with more than 200 public companies. No politics. No current events. Only Opportunities To Consider™.
